title: Musical family and the family piano
summary: Mother, siblings and brothers played piano, George trumpet; the family piano he practiced on until he sold it for $25, and his sister the nun.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My mother played, my older sister played, and my sister, the next to the older sister, played... What instrument? Piano. My oldest brother played piano. My next to the oldest brother played piano. Uh, my brother George, he played trumpet. Oh, somebody wants to see. I'll turn it off for a minute.
See, you were telling about all your family played piano. You had a piano right in your home then.

That's it. And, uh, the history of that piano, that piano, most of us learned on that one piano. I got rid of that piano in 1963. That's not so long ago now. Well, how long did you have it then? That piano stayed in the family. They bought that piano before I was born.
Oh, yeah. Because my sister— Four nineteen and eight then?

Yes. My sister, it was a Sharma. And it was a heavy thing, and when we moved on Broadway Street in the house, it was too heavy to bring up stairs, so we left it in the basement. And I used to play it, and practice on it, and play it, and practice on it, until the strings couldn't stand anymore. They told me the only thing that'd be done, left to be done with the piano was to have it restrown. I thought it was too expensive. Yeah. I sold it for $25. Sold it for $25. And get settled. Now, my youngest sister is a nun. She's been from Juilliard. Oh, really? She had a dear She's teaching my little girl music now, and she's a genius. And it was through her, when she was going to school at Xavier, after I left Xavier, around 1925, she was really stuck with the music. And so I started following her, and she started helping me a little bit. So the whole family knew Steve Lewis.
